discovery: Development of atom interferometry for precision measurement

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Université Paris 13 / LNE-SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Atom interferometry turned the wave nature of matter into a precision instrument. Bordé showed that atomic beam spectroscopy with separated laser fields is a matter-wave interferometer and built the theory of photon-recoil beam splitters. Pritchard's group built the first Mach-Zehnder interferometer for atoms with nanofabricated gratings and used it to measure atomic polarizabilities and decoherence. Kasevich, working with Chu, invented the light-pulse atom interferometer using stimulated Raman transitions, which gave gravimeters, gyroscopes and gradiometers with unprecedented sensitivity. Their work now underpins the most precise measurements of the fine-structure constant, tests of the equivalence principle at the 10^-12 level, measurements of Newton's constant, searches for dark energy and dark matter, and field-deployable quantum sensors. Few experimental techniques have yielded so many orders-of-magnitude gains in sensitivity and so many new laboratory tests of fundamental physics, each backed by a careful error budget.
